proof_summary: Write \(n=2^k m\) with \(m\) odd and group middle divisors by their odd part \(o\mid m\); successive multiples \(2^j o\) have squares differing by a factor of four, so exactly one is middle precisely when both \(o^2\) and \((m/o)^2\) are below \(2n\). Pairing divisors \(o\leftrightarrow m/o\) then shows that the non-middle contribution is counted twice by those complementary divisors whose square exceeds \(2n\).
